instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the macaroni. Add 1 tbsp of salt.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tsp of the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Cut 2 scallions into 2-inch pieces and slice 2 thin pieces of the ginger. Cook them for 1 minute, until lightly browned.
Add the broth, 2 cups water, the light soy sauce and the oyster sauce. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 20 minutes.
While the broth simmers, cook the macaroni for the time on the package. Drain it and set it aside.
Slice the ham into strips. Thinly slice the 2 remaining scallions.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Crack in the eggs and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.
Fish the ginger and scallion pieces out of the broth. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide the macaroni among 4 bowls. Top with the ham, ladle the hot broth over, and set a fried egg on each. Sprinkle with the sliced scallions.
method_notes: Every version online has under 20 ratings, so this follows The Seasoned Wok (5.0 from 1), which serves 4: ginger and scallion browned in oil, then chicken broth and water simmered with a little light soy and oyster sauce for 20 minutes. Macaroni, deli ham and a fried egg go in the bowl. tasteasianfood makes its own chicken-bone broth for an hour, which is too long for a lunch. Bought broth is used here.
